chunks: From him, from Aḥmad, from al-Barqī, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام: that he gave judgment concerning
a man who entered the house of a people without their permission and was injured. He said: “There is no liability upon them; but if he entered with their permission, they are liable.”

key_terms.فَعُقِرَ: then he was injured or wounded
key_terms.لَا ضَمَانَ: there is no legal liability or compensation

ai.seo_question: Is there legal liability if someone is injured after entering a house without permission?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability for injury in relation to entering a private home. If a person enters without permission and is harmed, the occupants bear no liability; but if he entered with their permission, they are responsible.
